findings.description: Granularity of staleness: EARS text says "mark the view stale" (singular, view-level). All three A outputs unanimously build a single per-view boolean/enum staleness state (A1's `ViewFreshness.stale: bool`, A2's `ViewStaleness(AtomicBool)`, A3's `ViewStatus` enum in one `Arc<Mutex<>>`) — directly forced by the spec's singular phrasing, and genuinely absent from the real code. The real `Publisher` (sheets-view/src/lib.rs) tracks staleness PER TAB via `stale: BTreeSet<String>` / `RepublishOutcome.stale_tabs: Vec<String>`: one of the four view tabs can fail and be marked stale while `republish`'s per-tab loop continues publishing the other three in the same cycle (see `failed_republish_marks_stale_writes_banner_and_retries` in tests/republish.rs, which only ever asserts/queries `POSITIONS_TAB` staleness independent of other tabs). All three B outputs correctly reconstruct this as per-tab independence (B1 item 1/5, B2 item 4/5, B3 item 3). This is the strongest finding: it is the same granularity gap surfacing from both directions at once — A implements the literal singular reading the spec text forces, B documents the actual per-tab reality the code enforces.

Advisory write-lock protocol: SHEET-PUB-003's text says nothing about a lock, another holder, or a non-destructive refusal path. Yet the real `Publisher::republish` acquires `lock.acquire()` BEFORE any tab mutation and, on `Err` (lock held elsewhere), returns immediately with `published:false`, writes nothing, and leaves the stale set exactly as it was before the call (lib.rs `republish`; tests `republish_acquires_the_lock_before_mutating` and `republish_under_a_held_lock_writes_nothing`). All three B outputs describe this precisely and consistently (B1 item 6, B2 item 8, B3 items 5-6: acquired-once, before-mutation, held-lock refuses non-destructively). None of the three A outputs invent any locking concept — correctly, since nothing in the given EARS text motivates it. This is a large, unanimous, pure B-side surplus.

`set_tab_order` failure semantics: the very existence of a trailing workbook tab-order reassert step, and the rule that its failure flips `RepublishOutcome.published` to `false` WITHOUT adding any tab to the stale set (order failures and per-tab publish failures tracked independently), is never stated in the EARS text — SHEET-PUB-003 talks only about "a republish" failing, not a two-part publish+reorder operation. B1 item 4, B2 item 6, and B3 item 4 all capture this exact independence rule with no disagreement. No A output anticipates a tab-ordering concept at all (nothing in the spec text motivates it), so this is pure B-side surplus.

Exact banner contract: the code pins the literal string `"STALE — last sync {stale_banner_quote_ts}"` (lib.rs `republish`) written to cell `'{tab}'!AA1` (runtime/src/adapters.rs `write_stale_banner`), verified in tests/republish.rs (`banner.contains("STALE")`, `banner.contains("2022-09-01")`). SHEET-PUB-003 says only "a best-effort in-tab banner" — no format, no cell location. B1 and B2 both capture the exact text string but omit the `AA1` cell address; only B3 (item 1) captures the cell reference — a real, if narrow, disagreement among the B runs on this specific granular constant.

Missing-tab-is-bootstrap-not-failure adapter policy: `ViewSheetsAdapter::batch_update_view` (runtime/src/adapters.rs), on a missing-tab error from the low-level primitive, treats it as fresh-workbook bootstrap (create sheet, write the frozen header once, retry the data write once) rather than a failure — only a sub-step failure inside that sequence surfaces as `ViewError::PublishFailed`. Nothing in the EARS text distinguishes a missing tab from any other write failure. B1 item 8, B2 item 10, and B3 items 9-10 all reconstruct this consistently and in detail — unanimous B-side surplus.

Settle-pass scope disagreement between B runs: B3 additionally folds in `republish_then_settle`'s strict after-write settle ordering (item 7) and both B1 (item 9) and B3 (item 11) describe `read_price_pass` failure mapping to `PublishFailed`, while B2 is silent on `read_price_pass` failure semantics entirely (its item 10 covers only the view-tab write path). This is a genuine B-internal scope disagreement about whether settle-pass/offline-read behavior belongs under "republish failure," separate from the otherwise-unanimous core findings above.

notes: Real code read directly: sheets-view/src/lib.rs (Publisher::republish/republish_then_settle, ViewError, SheetsViewClient), sheets-view/src/testkit.rs (InMemorySheetsView), sheets-view/tests/republish.rs, runtime/src/adapters.rs (ViewSheetsAdapter), runtime/tests/adapters.rs. All three A outputs converge tightly beyond the scored finding: structural (no-log-handle) enforcement of 'log unaffected' (correctly matches real code, which takes no store/log reference — not a drift), passive next-tick retry with no dedicated backoff/queue (matches code), and reading 'best-effort' as modifying only the banner (not the TUI) — this last point is a unanimous A-side interpretive choice but the real sheets-view crate has no TUI-notification code at all to compare against (only a pull-style Publisher::stale_tabs() getter), so it can't be confirmed as a code-side gap and is treated as an unfalsifiable assumption artifact, not a scored finding, per the classification instructions. All three A outputs also invent a push-style TUI notifier trait (notify_stale/notify_fresh) with no basis in the actual code (which only exposes a getter) — again an assumption artifact, not scored. B-side agreement is high on all core substantive requirements (per-tab stale set, lock gate, tab-order independence, missing-tab bootstrap) and only diverges on two narrow points (the AA1 cell constant, and whether settle-pass/offline-read semantics belong in scope), which is why bAgreement is rated high rather than medium despite findings 4 and 6 above.
